test_title: PYST 7: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Direct tax reforms are part of India's revenue consolidation strategy. Which committee recommended simplification of direct taxes in post-liberalization India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelkar Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kelkar Committee** was established in **2002** under the chairmanship of **Dr. Vijay Kelkar**. It was tasked with providing recommendations for simplifying and modernizing India's direct tax system.
 
• The committee aimed to streamline the tax structure, reduce exemptions, and ensure better compliance. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• It proposed measures to promote transparency, reduce tax evasion, and increase revenue collection through reforms in direct taxation.
 
• The Kelkar Committee suggested implementing **modern tax administration practices**, such as e-filing and e-payment, to make the system more efficient.
 
• The committee also recommended the removal of certain exemptions to simplify the tax structure, which would lead to broadening the tax base.
 
• One of its key suggestions was the adoption of a **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, which was eventually implemented in India in **2017**.
 
• The recommendations of the Kelkar Committee were instrumental in shaping India's tax reforms, particularly in the post-liberalization era.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Kelkar Committee.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Narasimham Committee:**

 
 
• The **Narasimham Committee**, set up in **1991** and **1998**, focused primarily on **banking sector reforms** in India.
 
• It recommended measures such as reducing government stake in banks, improving the capital adequacy ratio, and introducing asset reconstruction companies. This committee did not focus on direct tax reforms.
 
 
 
• **Tarapore Committee:**
 
 
• The **Tarapore Committee** was constituted in **1997** to recommend measures for **capital account convertibility** in India.
 
• Its recommendations were aimed at financial liberalization, but it did not deal with direct tax simplification.
 
 
 
• **Dutta Committee:**
 
 
• The **Dutta Committee**, headed by R.K. Dutta, focused on reforms in public sector enterprises and their management. It was not involved in direct tax reform recommendations.
 
 
 
• **Direct Tax Reforms:**
 
 
• Direct taxes include **income tax, corporate tax, and property tax**. Simplifying these taxes ensures better compliance and improved revenue collection.
 
• India has implemented multiple direct tax reforms, such as e-filing of returns, reduction in corporate tax rates, and introduction of **faceless assessment**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legacy of the Kelkar Committee:**

 
 
• The Kelkar Committee's recommendations laid the foundation for India’s modern tax reforms, including the implementation of **GST** and advancement in direct tax compliance measures.
 
• The committee emphasized the importance of minimizing tax exemptions and ensuring equity in taxation to promote economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Tax Reforms:**
 
 
• India has continually reformed its tax structure to align with global practices, improve compliance, and reduce the burden on taxpayers.
 
• Tax reforms like **Digital India initiatives** and **faceless assessment** reflect the modernization suggested by earlier committees like Kelkar.
